newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - December 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - December 16.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

President Chandrika Kumaratunga says she is prepared to stage constitutional revolution with support of people if she is unable to win a two-thirds majority in parliament to change constitution and implement devolution plan to end ethnic war.
President Kumaratunga refutes speculation of imminent split in cabinet of ministers. Government is stable despite a wafer-thin majority in parliament, she told public rally.
Army top brass have narrow escape after Tamil Tiger rebels fire at their helicopter over Unichchi jungles in east. The senior officers were going to supervise operations against rebels' jungle bases.
Leaders of 50 labour unions to meet on Monday to discuss labour union action over privatisation of Oruwela Steel Corporation. Unions say price at which Korean investors bought company was too cheap.
Military creates special operations and intelligence unit to fight Tamil rebel activity in Colombo.
Security forces report heavy fighting in operation to flush Tamil Tiger rebels out of their jungle lairs in east after guerrillas overran Pulukunava police commando base.
